orientation: This pull request configures a composite unique database index on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) in EF Core and updates PaymentService.PayAsync to handle duplicate and concurrent payment requests idempotently. The goal is to prevent customers from being double-charged upon retried or concurrent payment submissions as reported in support ticket #4711.

findings.title: Payment entity is placed on hold and never completed or persisted as successful
findings.claim: PaymentService calls payment.Hold() before saving the payment entity, but never transitions the payment to completed after the ledger transfers succeed. As a result, the payment remains in a held status in the database and is returned in an incomplete state to callers.
findings.requirement_link: When IPaymentService.PayAsync is called sequentially by the same customer with an IdempotencyKey that already exists for that CustomerId, it returns the existing first payment without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync or moving money again.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove payment.Hold() or update the payment state to completed and persist the changes after ILedger.PostTransferAsync operations succeed.

findings.title: Unique constraint exception handler fails to retrieve in-flight payment and throws
findings.claim: When a concurrent request catches a DbUpdateException unique constraint violation, the winning request is still executing ILedger transfers and has not yet committed its transaction. The losing request immediately queries for the existing payment via AsNoTracking, finds null because the winning transaction is uncommitted, and throws an unhandled exception instead of returning the payment.
findings.requirement_link: When two requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey execute concurrently, at most one payment record is persisted and ILedger.PostTransferAsync is called at most once (with decimal amount rounded using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); the second request handles the database unique constraint violation and returns the existing first payment rather than failing with an unhandled exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit or release the idempotency reservation record before moving to non-transactional ledger transfers, or implement a retry/poll mechanism to wait for the concurrent transaction to commit before querying.

votes.reason: The finding assumes an RDBMS will raise a unique constraint violation while the winning transaction is still in-flight and uncommitted. In all major relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL/InnoDB, SQL Server, Oracle), a concurrent insert conflicting on a unique constraint blocks waiting for the first transaction to complete; it only throws a unique constraint violation after the first transaction has committed. In SQLite, concurrent write transactions are serialized at the database lock level. Thus, the winning transaction is never still executing when the losing transaction catches the constraint violation.

findings.title: Unbounded static semaphore dictionary introduces stateful memory leak in application service
findings.claim: IdempotencyLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim instance for every processed customer and idempotency key without any removal or cache expiration policy. This introduces stateful in-process synchronization that will leak memory over time and does not coordinate across multi-instance API deployments.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> IdempotencyLocks = new();
findings.requirement_link: When two requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey execute concurrently, at most one payment record is persisted and ILedger.PostTransferAsync is called at most once (with decimal amount rounded using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); the second request handles the database unique constraint violation and returns the existing first payment rather than failing with an unhandled exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the static IdempotencyLocks semaphore map. Let concurrent executions attempt persistence and handle the database unique constraint violation as specified in the acceptance criteria.

findings.title: PaymentService leaks SQLite engine and connection-level locking into application layer
findings.claim: PaymentService imports Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and implements provider-specific write serialization via GetSqliteWriteLock and SQLite connection tracking. Application services should remain decoupled from underlying database engine implementations and let EF Core and database transactions manage concurrency.
findings.requirement_link: When two requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey execute concurrently, at most one payment record is persisted and ILedger.PostTransferAsync is called at most once (with decimal amount rounded using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); the second request handles the database unique constraint violation and returns the existing first payment rather than failing with an unhandled exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove SQLite-specific write locks and connection inspections from PaymentService. Rely on standard EF Core transaction management and DbUpdateException handling.

findings.title: Unbounded static dictionary IdempotencyLocks causes a memory leak
findings.claim: IdempotencyLocks stores a new SemaphoreSlim for every customerId and IdempotencyKey pair and never evicts or removes keys. Under ongoing production traffic, this static collection will grow monotonically and leak memory.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> IdempotencyLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Remove in-memory static semaphores in favor of database constraint enforcement, or ensure semaphores are removed from the dictionary after execution.

findings.title: Unbounded memory growth in static IdempotencyLocks dictionary
findings.claim: IdempotencyLocks stores a SemaphoreSlim for every unique customer and idempotency key combination but never removes them. In a long-running service, this static dictionary will grow indefinitely and leak memory.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> IdempotencyLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the semaphore entry when the operation finishes (or when no callers are queued) rather than accumulating entries permanently in a static dictionary.

findings.title: SQLite-specific concurrency workarounds coupled to application service
findings.claim: PaymentService inspects low-level database connection properties and maintains static SQLite file/connection locks inside GetSqliteWriteLock. Mixing database provider-specific synchronization into the application domain increases maintenance overhead and breaks separation of concerns.
findings.suggested_fix: Rely on database transaction semantics or isolate database-engine test workarounds outside the core PaymentService.

findings.title: Unbounded static ConcurrentDictionary leaks memory over time
findings.claim: The static dictionary `IdempotencyLocks` caches a `SemaphoreSlim` for every processed idempotency key without any removal, TTL, or eviction. In a long-running service processing continuous payment traffic, this causes unbounded memory growth.
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> IdempotencyLocks = new();
findings.requirement_link: When two requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey execute concurrently, at most one payment record is persisted and ILedger.PostTransferAsync is called at most once
findings.suggested_fix: Clean up entries when processing completes (e.g., via `TryRemove`), or rely on the unique database constraint and transaction isolation rather than an unbounded static dictionary.

findings.title: Redundant duplicate query for existing payment on execution path
findings.claim: PaymentService queries the database for existing payments with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey at lines 173-175 under the lock, and then executes the exact same query again at lines 226-228 inside ExecuteIdempotentPaymentAsync without any intervening state change, introducing redundant database round-trips.
findings.requirement_link: When IPaymentService.PayAsync is called sequentially by the same customer with an IdempotencyKey that already exists for that CustomerId, it returns the existing first payment without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync or moving money again.
findings.suggested_fix: Eliminate the second query in ExecuteIdempotentPaymentAsync and rely on the result checked immediately beforehand in PayAsync.

findings.title: Consecutive redundant database round-trips reloading account balance
findings.claim: The method reloads `fromAccount` from the database via ReloadAsync and then immediately queries Accounts a second time for Balance and AllowOverdraft. This creates two consecutive round-trips to read the same account state on every payment.
findings.suggested_fix: Use either ReloadAsync or the projected AsNoTracking query to inspect the latest account balance, rather than executing both.

findings.title: Unbounded memory growth in static IdempotencyLocks dictionary (Resource Exhaustion)
findings.claim: PaymentService registers a SemaphoreSlim in the static dictionary IdempotencyLocks for every distinct customer and idempotency key combination. Because entries are never evicted or removed after the lock is released, untrusted user-supplied idempotency keys accumulate indefinitely, leading to memory exhaustion and denial of service (CWE-400).
findings.evidence: private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> IdempotencyLocks = new();
findings.suggested_fix: Evict the key from IdempotencyLocks once execution completes, or rely on database-level unique constraints and transactions for concurrency control rather than an unbounded static cache.
